newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Vranitzky ready to resign, paper says.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Vranitzky ready to resign, paper says.

text.p: One of Austria's most respected daily newspapers reported on Saturday that Chancellor Franz Vranitzky would resign this weekend and be succeeded by Finance Minister Viktor Klima.
There was no independent confirmation of the report in Der Standard but Vranitzky, 59, has repeatedly been said to have become tired of politics after his 10 years in the chancellery.
Nobody at Vranitzky's or Klima's offices was immediately available for comment.

The paper said Vranitzky had told senior members of his Social Democratic party, which rules in a coalition with the conservative People's Party, that he wanted to resign. He was likely to announce his resignation after another high-level meeting of party executives on Sunday evening, it added.
A former banker and professional basketball player, Vranitzky became chancellor in 1986 after two years at the finance ministry.
The paper said a successor for current Finance Minister Viktor Klima, also a Social Democrat, had not yet been chosen.
But according to a report in the popular daily Kurier, Klima would be replaced by felow Social Democrat Rudolf Scholten, Minister for Transport and Telecommunications.

The Social Democrats and the conservatives last weekend struck a deal on the sale of the state's controlling stake in flagship bank Creditanstalt to arch-rival Bank Austria, after a bitter dispute that threatened to split the coalition.

The coalition was formed after a snap election in December of last year after the conservatives quit the previous government following a heated row over how to cut the country's growing budget deficit.
